status: PROPOSAL — staged. The other two thirds of SNG-266, with Erik's approved level-curve fix.

1_narrativeTaper.where: content/packs/core/rules/resolution.json → rules.xp (EDIT of a live block, not a new file)
reasoning: HALVE THE BASE BAND, KEEP novelBonus AT 8. Erik: 'you should still get some.' The base band is paid for ANY resolved action, so it is what compounds; the novel bonus is paid for doing something genuinely NEW, which is exactly the narrative play worth rewarding. Tapering the first and protecting the second targets the actual problem.

sceneSoftCap 20: past 20 narrative XP in one scene, further awards drop to 1. THIS IS THE REAL FIX for talking-out-levels-doing — it does not punish long scenes, it stops them COMPOUNDING. A player can still roleplay for an hour; they just cannot out-earn a quest by doing it.
⚠️ AND IT ONLY WORKS WITH THE SCENE BOUNDARY (part 3). A per-scene cap on an unbounded scene is not a cap. The two ship together or neither does.

2_levelCurve.where: content/packs/core/rules/resolution.json → rules.leveling (ADD a field) + progression.js:70 (one-line read)
2_levelCurve.current: while (character.xp >= character.level * per) — ALREADY linear-rising; L1→2 = 100, L99→100 = 9,900, cumulative to L100 ≈ 495,000

effect.L1-L40: UNCHANGED — the early and mid game feel exactly as they do today
effect.L41-L100: flat 4,000 per level instead of rising to 9,900
effect.whatItFixes: linear-per-level makes TOTAL cost quadratic; the last ten levels alone cost ~95,000 — a fifth of the whole game for 10% of the levels. The cap removes the wall without touching the part that already works.

whyThisShapeAndNotAnother: It is ONE LINE and one rules field. Nothing else in the engine reads the threshold.
It preserves the early curve EXACTLY, which is the part Erik said he liked ('easier in the first levels').
It degrades safely: if levelCostCap is absent, the formula is identical to today's. An old save or an unpatched rules file behaves exactly as before.

A tier-banded alternative (novice 80 / adept 150 / master 400 / heroic 900 / legendary 2000) is MORE authorable and ties to SNG-260's powerBands — worth revisiting if Erik later wants per-band pacing control. Not needed for the fix.

3_sceneBoundary.where: engine/gm.js (directive) + app.js scene handling — CCODE'S HALF
3_sceneBoundary.theFinding: The GM ALREADY owns scene-ending and gm.js:86 already carries the full doctrine ('a scene is a UNIT, not the session'). Nothing needs re-designing. What is missing is a FLOOR and a CEILING — and SCENE_TURN_CAP is bounded STORAGE only (slice(-CAP)); it trims the array and DOES NOT end the scene, so a scene can run forever while quietly forgetting its own beginning.

proposed.softCloseBehaviour: the GM's turn context gains a line: 'this scene has run 8 beats — find the honest close within the next two.' A NUDGE. The GM still picks the moment, which preserves the existing doctrine that a scene must never end mid-action.
proposed.hardCloseBehaviour: the engine sets sceneEnded itself and asks the GM only for the sceneSummary. MUST defer to the end of the current resolution — never mid-action, never mid-sentence, never with a question hanging.
proposed.theButton: KEEP as an override — a player should always be able to say 'this is done' — but it stops being the primary path. Erik is right that a manual control for something the system should do itself is a workaround.

ccodeNeeds: ⚠️ REGISTER rules/encounters.json in content/packs/core/manifest.json under provides.rules. THE FILE DOES NOTHING WITHOUT THIS — and that is precisely how the bug survived.
app.js:2794 → read `rules.encounters[type] || rules.encounters.default` so a new type can never silently pay zero again.
Implement threat-ratio scaling + the walkAway and incapacitated FORMULAS (they are situational, not flat).
The per-scene narrative cap and the soft/hard scene closes.

⚠️ THE VERIFICATION THAT MATTERS IS A SESSION-SHAPE SIM, not per-award: model 1 quest + 2 encounters + ~15 narrative actions at three bands and report the SHARE each source contributed. Target 45/35/15/5. INVARIANT: a player who does one quest and two encounters must out-earn a player who does neither and talks for the same wall-clock time. Today they LOSE to them.
